about: Public-notice channels per operator or agency: pages, sites, feeds, lists and accounts through which the public is told of sewage discharges, by law, permit or voluntarily. Read by pipeline/ingest/notification_pages.py (schema and validator there; test tests/test_notice_channels.py).

channels.name: 145th Street Water and Sewer Improvement District No. 345 of Pulaski County
channels.legal_basis: NPDES permit AR0040266, Part II, as DEQ states it on its incident page: "Notification must be made within 24 hours of becoming aware of the circumstances, and in most cases, an additional 5-Day Written Report is required for the following occurrences: ... Any Sanitary Sewer Overflow (SSO), no matter how small ... Any Unpermitted Discharge from either a collection or treatment system, regardless of whether it reaches waters of the state"
channels.note: 145th Street Water and Sewer Improvement District No. 345 of Pulaski County reports every sanitary sewer overflow, unanticipated bypass, upset and unpermitted discharge to DEQ within 24 hours on its online forms (in most cases with a five-day written report); DEQ publishes the report in its Reported Noncompliance Incident Data search, usually the next day, read by the ar-deq-overflow-incidents feed.

channels.name: 145th Street Water and Sewer Improvement District No. 345 of Pulaski County
channels.note: No URL known (not searched individually): no Arkansas rule requires a permittee to tell the public of an overflow, and this operator's own pages were not searched, so whether it posts notices online is not known. DEQ's form has a 'Public Notification' box among the actions taken; the search shows the tick, not the notice.

channels.name: Arkansas Department of Health, Arkansas Swim Beach Program
channels.note: The Swim Beach Program page lists the swim beaches the Department has closed, by its SB number and name (one on 2026-11-14), with no date, reason, water or point. Read each run by the ar-adh-swim-beach-status feed. (ar-adh-swim-beach-status)

channels.note: The file behind DEQ's Harmful Algal Blooms page and its archive: 52 recreational use health advisories since 2014 with the days posted and lifted, county and nearest town (4 in effect on 2026-11-14). Read each run by the ar-deq-hab-advisories feed. (ar-deq-hab-advisories)

channels.name: Arkansas Division of Environmental Quality, Office of Water Quality
channels.note: DEQ's Reported Noncompliance Incident Data search: every SSO, bypass, upset and unpermitted discharge filed on its 24-hour online forms, usually by the next day, with the days it started and stopped, the volume, the filer's impact and a location text, but no coordinates, county or receiving water (2,449 reports from 2025-01-01 to 2026-11-14). A form search with no export endpoint; no rule requires DEQ to publish it. Read each run by the ar-deq-overflow-incidents feed. (ar-deq-overflow-incidents)
